✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Why not include Reverse and Shortest, too?

It's a nice exercise for a clash, but you may need to increase the number of given digits and the min/max, maybe allow negative numbers?
It will block, like Cakeisalie5 said, "brute-force" solutions with a loop or something else, forcing the use of a sort function (if it was intended).
I also think you may enable reverse and shortest -- it will also work very well!

Hey! The exercise is not super original, but looking at your solution, I'm thinking maybe it might be necessary for some people. Can you make the maximum for each number e.g. 2 billion, and make the final numbers something like 4, 4564, 948498 and 1854126894? This will eliminate solutions that go through every number between the minimum and the maximum, since it would time out.
I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!
This is not an improvement, but rather, a suggestion. Why not enable shortest and reverse as well? I think they would be suitable for all three game modes.
Easy clash, relevant to beginners. Please rephrase the Goal as "Sort the given numbers from smallest to largest."
very nice for someone who's just starting

Formatting
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly as described in the points below.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement, e.g. write answer.

Input
* Please format "Line 1", "Line 2", etc. in <<bold>>.

* Please format A, B, C and D as [[variables]].

* Please remove "random" from all the descriptions.

Output
* Please format the line numbers in <<bold>>.

* Some line numbers are incorrect.

Constraints
* Please format A, B, C and D as [[variables]].

Cases
* Each test and validator should cover the same scenario, using different inputs and outputs. Currently, the cases don't seem to target specific scenarios. Please revise them as follows:

  • Test/Validator 1: A, B, C and D are all distinct, with A being the largest.

  • Test/Validator 2: A, B, C and D are all distinct, with B being the largest.

  • Test/Validator 3: A, B, C and D are all distinct, with C being the largest.

  • Test/Validator 4: A, B, C and D are all distinct, with D being the largest.

  • Test/Validator 5: Two of the four integers are equal.

  • Test/Validator 6: Three of the four integers are equal.

  • Test/Validator 7: All four integers are equal.

* Please also use more random integers as inputs; there are currently too many single-digit integers.

Thanks.

Thank you for following up my earlier comment. There are just a few remaining points:

Constraints
* Please format A, B, C and D as [[variables]] separately, excluding the commas.

* Test 5: Please change 39 to 1, so that the input consists of two numbers each appearing twice, similar to Validator 5.

* Validator 6: Please remove the trailing newline from the input.

Thanks again.
